decisions.decision: Serial wave execution with verification gates
decisions.rationale: High-risk infrastructure changes (BaseAgent lifecycle, DB pools) require isolation between waves

decisions.decision: Renaissance design from 4 to 9 HYGIENE criteria
decisions.rationale: Architectural weakness assessment identified 9 measurable criteria across Service Consistency (30%), Silent Failure Elimination (35%), Complexity Reduction (35%)
Objective success measurement - each criterion returns TRUE/FALSE
Allow Grafana monitoring to detect anomalies before proceeding

high_priority: Service inventory gap - need proof all 42+ services covered
Verification specificity gap - need rollback criteria + failure-mode testing
Wave 3 scope creep risk - bundles too many changes (DAG + SQL + dead code + docs)
medium_priority: Missing service-by-service acceptance evidence (SIGTERM, stall detection, DB pool closure)
agreed_strengths: Serial wave execution is appropriate and well-justified
Binary SQL verification is a strong design choice

context_notes: Phase 107 planning complete. Cross-AI review surfaced 5 consensus concerns (3 HIGH, 2 MEDIUM). Plans are technically sound with MEDIUM-HIGH overall risk. Serial wave strategy validated by both reviewers. Main risk is false closure - marking criteria complete while some services/paths remain uncovered. Reviewer recommendation: add service inventory, verification matrix, rollback criteria, and failure-path tests before execution.
